reviews.comment: Great professor, was very funny and gave extra credit opportunities as well. Only thing was that the exam was very difficult but other than that, the class overall was great.

Neither this professor nor the lecture is the problem. It is the lab and the overall department. Check your lab group submissions; they will gpa game you. TAs are a dice roll, and don't expect any support from them or the department. Lectures weren't perfect but better than I expected. Exams are still ridiculously difficult for what's taught.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Class had lots of individual and group assignments, so it's important to stay on top of your work. Extra credit is very important to do, and will really boost your final grade. The exams were fairly challenging, so study a week or more in advance. Overall, good professor.

If you have experience with coding, you will do well on individual HW and exams. The groups you are paired with can definitely make or break the team assignments. Overall, professor Susindar offers a ton of extra credit throughout the semester. She does offer engaging lectures, but exam is common so it can be difficult to know how to study.

Tough class (mostly because of the final exam) but awesome professor. She cares about the students and always make sure that everyone in the class understand the materials. Gives extra credits and drop a few assignments.

She was a good professor, it's just a difficult class for some. Her lectures can be a bit abstract at times for very specific concepts. There's a homework every week along with a quiz that is posted at odd times.   Overall an alright professor, better than most.
This is a weird class, but Susindar makes sure you're prepared for the final.
Homework got easier the last few weeks which was very thoughtful, and overall the course wasn't bad. Would recommend.

The professor is probably one of the most generous with extra credit for ENGR 216. This semester (it might change), she dropped the two lowest daily grades (homework and quizzes) and gave an additional 1% to the overall grade. The class itself is hard, but her generous grading made the A not require too much effort (still required a lot).

She tries to teach and cares about her students. The course is poorly designed and difficult, but Professor Susindar tries to ensure students get an A. The final is extremely difficult, but she offers a lot of extra credit and may curve. There are pop quizzes!
reviews.ratingTags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: i hate this class and i'm projecting my feelings into her. i never looked both ways on my way to this class.

Eng 216 is a weird class overall, so honestly prof dosent matter. Susindar definitely prepared the class for the final with many in class assignments. Her in class midterm and practice final in class were very helpful towards the final. Honestly, the final wasn't dreadful, but it definitely wasn't easy!
not in much of a hurry to do anything

She is so hot. I used to go to her class early just to get a glimpse of her radiating smile. My roommates were in the class, but I  used to abandon them to see Susindar. She is so cute and hot and feminine and i want to be submissive to her.

a really awesome professor! it's easy to tell that she cares a lot about her students, and she does a lot to make sure that students succeed. she gives a lot of homework and has pretty strict formatting standards, but i honestly didn't think it was that bad. let us do midterm corrections for full points back
Tough class, decent professor, just moves oo fast with lecture material and reads off slides.

Definitely a good prof and a good person, cares a lot abt her students and takes the time to answer questions. She is very patient with those who may struggle. 216 is a poorly structured class but she tries to make it easier on her students. Would love to take her again

216 is a rough class, but Dr Susindar is very understanding and transparent with students and does everything she can to prepare you for the final. The work is not hard and many of the things she does, like the HW format and inclass midterm, are there to help students especially since she offers inclass bonus and midterm corrections to full credit.

Look, 216 is a poorly structured class, but Dr Susindar actually cares about your success, just unfortunate that she had to teach the worst possible classes. Took both her 102 and 216 Easy B if you do all the work and get at least 2 questions right on the final. I would take her again

Decent at lectures, but she makes the class super easy with the coding assignments and plenty of extra credit. Quizzes aren't too difficult. Tests aren't easy, but if you do proper preparation they're not bad at all. Also quite entertaining and likes hearing student feedback.

my intelligence is fairly average for tamu engr. the homework after the first couple weeks is hard. my friends w/ diff profs have less hw problems, less obnoxious format requirements, and much more flexible due dates. takes over a week to respond to emails. everyone fails the final so making everything else also difficult is obnoxious.
mid, hw easy, learning nothing
Lectures are really boring, only class doing a handwritten midterm, not a fan of her teaching had to self study a lot

The professor isn't the problem, the class is. She tries her best to teach and is very nice, but her teaching is nothing great. The class is difficult for people who are coding for the first time. If you just study hard for the exams, the class will be curved, and she is very generous and gives lots of extra credit so you'll be fine.

She's the best honestly! Her way of teaching made it super engaging to learn. The class itself is highly difficult but you have a lot of resources to use and she gives you a lot to practice. Coming from someone who had NO expierence with coding whatsoever, super fun. Do all the extra credit, don't forget it really helps boost your final grade.

Dr. Susindar was great. She did her best to make class engaging and was good at giving examples and walking through concepts. Quizzes were easy; just review the slides/zybooks before class. Common exams were very difficult, so do all the extra credit she offers, which is a lot. She wants you to succeed, so don't be afraid to ask questions.

102 is a hard class period but I think she was a great prof overall. Lectures were easy to follow along for the most part and she gave extra credit opportunities throughout the year (DO ALL OF THEM!!! I didn't which separated me from a B to an A. She's really fun overall despite the class itself but I would recommend!

The class was pretty easy due to prior coding experience. It is very important to do all the bonuses that she gives you as it boosts your grades by a large margin. Also, another poster said that she didn't curve the final score, but I'm pretty sure that she did. It's probably a good idea to do the labs in advance. The tests were fine.

Good prof, caring towards students and acknowledges them individually if they need help. the tests were pretty difficult if you dont have a good background in coding, but she does a good job in trying to make her students learn. the curve did barely nothing to my grade

If you have 0 experience coding then DO NOT TAKE HER! She runs through lecture slides providing basic examples throughout and can be boring. You would be better off going through lecture slides and doing ZyBook modules on your own than going to class. The 2 tests are tedious and heavily weighed on your grade with low averages (40-70) and NO CURVE!
reviews.ratingTags: EXTRA CREDIT--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment:
If you do not know how to code in python this class may be a struggle. That being said susindar's extra credit is so good that it doesnt really matter lol. Her lectures are a bit boring but they are good for studying. The quizes are a lil difficult but finishable in 5 minutes. 
The tests are difficult so make sure you prep and comment for the TAs.

Dr Susindar was a good professor. I dont care for coding and she made it understandable and somewhat enjoyable. MAKE SURE TO DO THE EXTRA CREDIT. If you do bad on the first exam the EC will carry you. Exams arent too hard, just do the homeworks and quizzes. Good Prof, Will take again for 216

Dr Susindar is responsive, addresses individual concerns and responds to emails quickly. Her class included quizzes, individual and group labs, and exams. Exams were difficult but the same between sections so not Dr Susindars fault. I didn't find her teaching of class content to be that helpful but the resources available made achieving an A doable

Very test heavy course with low average (5-70) across sections, and does not curve them. Highschool level python course if you have previous coding experience. Coding lab (group) and quiz every week, but the lab is possible to do by yourself if you are experienced. Does not curve any grades but gives extra credit which is a lot of work
So Good. The class was a bit tough, but she's super nice. and HOT
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: 102 professors don't really matter but she was pretty chill. Good teacher not bad

ENGR 216 is a tough class, but I found that the difficulty came from the lab portion (and of course the final). Dr. Susindar does a great job of making the lecture portion engaging. I felt like I had a good understanding of the concepts. The homework can be annoying, but she structures it better than other Honors profs, and it ultimately did help.

216 at Texas A&M has to be the final boss of weed out courses. Any hiccup with professor Susindars rating in general is likely due to the nature of 216. She was passionate and ready to help when we didn't understand the content. She did her best to make the required course fun and engaging. Don't underestimate the final exam.

Dr. Susindar is a great professor. I enjoyed the class and would recommend this professor for ENGR 216. The class is organized well, and the homework is easy. Labs were easy and are 50% of your overall grade. The two lowest HW/Quiz grades are dropped.

I appreciate Dr. Susindar for rounding my final grade to an A. 

Take Dr. Susindar for ENGR 216.

She has bad ratings but was actually a good professor for 216 imo. She tries to include little jokes in her lectures, so they weren't as boring as the reviews said. She also was a HUGE help to my grade (in addition to my awesome lab TAs ofc) because she dropped 2 lowest grades and rounded up my grade to an A even tho the syllabus didn't mention it.
reviews.ratingTags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Susindar is really as good as you can get for the class that 216 is. If you go to class (you have to), talk to her, participate, and put your best work forward, you will succeed. The final is awful.

Good professor, she was kind and her lectures weren't bad. She was just held back by the horribly designed course that is ENGR 216. If you're registering for 216, I would recommend her. I had like a 94 going into the final and BOMBED it, which resulted in a B because of how absurdly hard it was. Otherwise, the course wasn't that bad.

Professor Susindar was incredibly hypercritical of any work submitted and disrespectful towards students, even in their success. Always found a way to criticize your learning while providing mid/useless lectures. Often skipped through many slides and didn't cover all material. Got one of the highest final scores and still don't like her one bit.

Good professor who may or may not be held back by the classes organization as a whole. Does her best with the lectures and does a good enough job. test heavy class, pretty much everyone has an A going into the final, but many will not end with an A.

I really liked Professor Susindar's lectures- she'd always incorporate small jokes to lighten up the class. Her FAQs on the homework assignments were also helpful. I didn't find the class that hard but I did self study a lot though.
Dr. Saya was a fun and engaging processor; she was always willing to help anyone who needed it and was very approachable which helped her feel more connected with us.
This course was really fun and got me way more interested in coding. I like how she would demonstrate coding through examples rather than just lecture slides.

Dr. Susindar is not a bad professor; her lectures and slides are pretty solid. But, overall, I felt like I could've used more demonstrations and feedback from her, but in reality, it felt like I was pretty much on my own for most of the time. Her exams are pretty tough even if there are only two of them.

She is an amazing teacher for 216!! Her lectures are to the point and give you all of the information that you need to know. The homework assignments are easy if you pay attention and made the midterm feel like a walk in the park.

Lectures were short and struggled to explain the concepts and will tell class to figure it out on their own, dont take her if youre new to coding (also doesnt respond to emails).Read lect slides on your own to do good on the quizzes and make sure to start the zybooks (will be extra credit) and labs early. Department exams are tough so practice alot
she was a little boring during lectures but when asked questions, was very helpful in her answers. Wants you to be successful so don't be afraid to ask questions

If you've never coded before, don't take Susindar. She often struggled to explain concepts during lectures, and sometimes gave up and told us to learn by experimenting ourselves. She wasn't terrible, but I read the lecture slides myself and feel like it was more effective than listening to her. If you have coded before, Susindar isn't a bad choice.

This class is easy with previous coding knowledge (I knew Java not Python but it was still easy).  Quizzes aren't too bad, labs should be easy 100s (start them early) and exams are similar to quizzes, maybe a little harder. Prof gave two generous extra credit assignments. Only negative is that sometimes she made multiple mistakes during lectures

Lectures were very short and not very clear, and she often asked the class for help during them. There are individual and team assignments, which have very clear instructions and grading criteria. Weekly quizzes, some harder than others. Tests are across the department but they are hard and had some topics not covered in lectures.
reviews.ratingTags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Eh, just eh. Susindar didn't really teach me much. The homework varied in difficulty a bunch from week to week. Some were free, others were monumentally harder. She does give decent reviews for the midterm and final but those are still very challenging. I don't know if any other 216 prof is better, but in general I wouldn't recommend her.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She is not necessarily a bad professor, but she honestly doesn't do that much. I think most of the help I got came from the TAs who would occasionally lead class when she wasn't there. She would occasionally leave half way through class when she was done lecturing and we were working on labs. Would have problems with her own code and need help.

Overall, the class is hard in general with little coding experience. However, Susindar is open and willing to work with the students of her class. Coding is something that has be somewhat learned through personal experience, but she is a great professor overall and puts in effort to provide extra credit assignments.

Dr. Susindar is a great professor and a lovely person. Although PHY/ENGR 216 is among my least favorite classes due to its strange structure as a standalone lab course with its own lecture, Dr. Susindar made the lectures enjoyable and a pleasure to attend every week.

Majority of the classes was graded by quizzes and homework. Lectures cant teach you much. She would sometimes get stuck on her own problems and have to consult the other professors. Quizzes were not similar to homework and there is absolutely no leniency on late work. Also there is random attendance checks.

If you already have a little bit of coding background and enjoy short lectures while having the rest of the class to work on the coding labs, Professor Susindar is the one for you. She's also great at answering questions when you have them.

She is terrible. Her lectures could not be any worse. The class is two hours long and she spends 20 minutes "teaching" and then lets you go to work on lab. Often times during that short, unhelpful lecture, the class is laughing at her for how confusing she is. She asks the class to help her figure out what she's doing wrong in her own lecture.

Not sure why her reviews are so low. She's a caring prof who's lectures are admittedly quite boring, but helpful and in depth. You don't even need to pay attention to the lectures to do well in this class, just have a general understandings of what's going on in your physics class and you'll be fine. Final is pretty rough though so prepare.
Dr. Saya is a nice person and good professor too. Lectures are short and interesting. HW is hard but you learn more from doing HW. I was well prepared for the "scary" final.
Professor Susindar is very friendly and professional. I felt very comfortable to ask questions and enjoyed lecture.

I would not recommend, but if you get her stay on top of homework and self study.
Again look for a different professor.

Absolutely horrendous, she rambles for 50 mins straight, does not respond to emails even if you have the correct format, the homework is a lot compared to other sections and is a tough grader. She does not give feedback. The only good thing is her slides and the TA( god sent). The final was ok, but its a lot of self study.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: 216 is easily the worst class at A&M, and it's meant to lower your GPA as the final is near impossible to pass. Professor Susindar gets a bad rep, but she isn't as bad as she seems. The Lab reports get easier with time and the homeowrks will take you roughly 3-4 hours. But again she is not awful, but could make 216 a lot more enjoyable.
reads off of lecture slides, boring lectures. doesn't explain concepts well. only way to survive is by watching other profs lectures. dont take

Shes so annoying to listen to, she takes forever to grade, she just drones on and on about the most useless things, she is whole reason why im switching out of engineering despite having a 4.0. AVOID HER LIKE THE PLAGUE
horrible lecturer drones on forever

Taking Dr. Susindar for ENGR 216 was very enjoyable. She does not assign hard homework, and makes it very easy to max out the assignment points in the class. The final is decently difficult, but it is a common exam, so taking any other professor would make the final the same. Overall pretty easy to get an A in the class.

Provides helpful lecture slides that make doing weekly HW simple. I only went to 3 classes and skipped the rest but still got 100s on all my HW by learning from the slides. The final is not that bad, just do the big review they give you and work out practice problems.
reviews.ratingTags: Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: i dont know why the reviews are bad. her lectures are yes boring and do not help much for the homeworks. honestly, your physics class associated with this class is what will help. homeworks are every week and a quiz but they just take time. there is a final that kills everyone but its meant to do that, she has no control over it to be honest.

Susindar isn't as bad as a lot of people make her out to be, when she's just reading off the slides it's pretty boring, but when she actually works out problems by hand its quite helpful and interesting. However, 216 is just a poorly organized class regardless of professor. Labs and homework are extremely time consuming but graded easily.

She is not very good at teaching the material in a way that makes the homework easy to understand. I regularly spend upwards of 3-4 hours per each weekly five question homework, but that may just be because the class is difficult. Homework is graded semi quickly. Do good on the labs and the homework and the final won't destroy your grade.
reads straight from power point, speaks very softly so she's hard to hear, literally only 1 test the entire semester

she seriously makes u question if industrial engineering is remotely even interesting. boring lectures, no feedback, powerpoints copied from other professor's. 

tldr: young prof with some enthusiam but zero teaching skills. if u want to succeed take someone else
Can be a tough class. But very accessible professor. Helped me greatly with my doubts and queries
Class was less boring than expected and its only 50 minutes. Professor is more helpful outside of class in office hours.

She seemed to not care much about teaching the course as she never was accessible outside of class. She just read straight off of slides and left me unprepared to take the final. Ended up getting curved a little, so it's whatever. Homeworks were harder than lecture examples and often felt lost. Definitely was my least favorite class this year.

Lectures were seemingly thrown together and had typos and grades were extremely slow to get back. I never received a response to an email until I copied the TA on the email. We basically received no feedback at all. She refused to post the final exam grades or answers with the only way of getting feedback being setting a meeting with her in June.

This review is for ISEN 360. 
She does not know how to effectively communicate. She does not reply to emails, at the end of the course wouldn't discuss grades until the next month. She does not know how to write or use spell check. Exams and assignments were full of typos and incomplete sentences or otherwise confusing wording.

Young professor with little teaching experience, but is eager to teach and has a great enthusiasm. Often times it seems like she does not know the material she is teaching. I went to all of her classes, but feel like I could have done just as well without attending a single one. Read the power points, and you will do fine.

This course is confusing no matter who you take it with, and Dr. Saya's mediocre lecturing skills don't help. Her explanations are convoluted and her handwriting is borderline incomprehensible. She is approachable before/after class to answer questions and during office hours, which does help.
Doesn't answer emails, can't read her handwriting
Tough class but great professor. Also open to answering questions at any time.
Really helpful. Can be a bit strict with grading and tests, but fantastic class to attend
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Inspirational
